title: Cova vs Flowhub: 2026 Dispensary POS Comparison
summary: Cova vs Flowhub compared for 2026: compliance, inventory, the new native e-commerce on both platforms, delivery gaps, and what an all-in-one replaces.
body_markdown:
Cova and Flowhub are both established dispensary POS systems, and the real comparison is no longer about which one has an online menu. Both now run native e-commerce. The decision comes down to how much of your stack each one covers on its own, and where you will still be paying a second vendor, which for most operators means delivery logistics.


**This guide compares Cova and Flowhub on compliance, inventory, e-commerce, delivery, and daily usability, then shows what changes when those jobs live in one platform.**

#### Key Takeaways


- Cova and Flowhub both offer native e-commerce that syncs with the POS in real time, so an online menu is no longer a point of difference between them.
- Cova sells its online store as a separate product from the core POS plan, which means the e-commerce line lands on a different invoice than the POS line.
- Both platforms handle delivery orders, but neither carries dispatch, routing, and live driver tracking end to end, so delivery operators add a logistics partner such as Carrot or Onfleet.
- Neither platform supports dynamic delivery, the model where drivers carry inventory and fulfill orders on the road rather than returning to the store between runs.
- Meadow includes e-commerce and both hub-and-spoke and dynamic delivery in the platform fee, and holds a 4.9 out of 5 rating across 90 G2 reviews as of October 2026.

## Key Features to Evaluate in Dispensary Software


Cova and Flowhub overlap on most of the basics, so a useful comparison focuses on the five areas where the two platforms actually diverge:


- **Compliance:** How much Metrc work is automated, and how much is left for your team?
- **Inventory:** Are counts accurate, and do they sync in real time across every menu?
- **E-Commerce:** Is the online store native, and does it come with the POS or on a separate line?
- **Delivery:** What does the platform handle itself, and where does a second vendor start?
- **User Experience:** Is it fast on the floor and workable in the back office?


---


## Cova POS Overview


Cova is a dispensary software provider headquartered in Denver, CO, and Vancouver, BC, serving cannabis retailers across the U.S. and Canada. The platform covers point of sale, inventory management, compliance, reporting, and payments, with an open API and a large integration catalog. Cova added a native online store, Cova eCommerce, in late 2022, and it is sold as an addition to the core POS plan rather than bundled into it.


### Cova's Key Features


- **Compliance Tools:** Two-way Metrc integration with automated sales reporting and inventory adjustments.
- **Inventory Management:** Real-time tracking, batch scanning, bulk updates, and reorder forecasting.
- **E-Commerce:** Cova eCommerce, a native online store that syncs inventory and pricing with the POS, sold separately from the core POS plan.
- **Payment Processing:** Cashless transactions through Cova Pay.
- **Point-of-Sale:** In-store, pickup, and delivery orders, with offline mode for connectivity drops.


### Cova Strengths


- **Regulatory Compliance:** Two-way Metrc sync handles sales reporting and adjustment reason codes automatically.
- **Inventory Depth:** Batch scanning, bulk adjustments, and room-level segmentation for multi-area stores.
- **Integration Catalog:** An open API with established connections to Weedmaps, Leafly, Alpine IQ, Springbig, and others.


### Cova Weaknesses


- **E-Commerce Is a Separate Product:** Cova eCommerce is priced and sold apart from the POS plan, so the online store is an added line rather than part of what the POS already includes.
- **Delivery Logistics Depend on Partners:** Cova handles delivery orders on the same inventory and compliance ledger as in-store sales, but Cova's own guidance points retailers to a dedicated logistics partner such as Carrot for dispatch and live vehicle tracking at scale.
- **No Dynamic Delivery:** There is no support for the model where drivers carry inventory and sell from the vehicle, so operators running that model need software that does.
- **Speed and Reliability:** Operators report long lag times and occasional system crashes, which bite hardest during peak hours.

## Flowhub POS Overview


Flowhub, founded in 2015, is a dispensary platform built around retail speed and compliance, best known for Nug, its handheld scanner for customer check-in and inventory counts. Flowhub[launched a POS-native e-commerce product in July 2025](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/flowhub-launches-pos-native-ecommerce-solution-to-power-online-cannabis-retail-growth-302503602.html) with live inventory sync, the same discount and tax engine the POS uses, and ACH pre-payment on online orders. Flowhub Delivery handles store-based delivery runs with Metrc manifests generated automatically, and pairs with Onfleet for the driver-side routing and tracking layer.


### Flowhub's Key Features


- **Nug:** Handheld scanning for check-in, ID verification, and inventory management.
- **E-Commerce:** POS-native online ordering with live inventory sync and ACH pre-payment.
- **Delivery:** Store-based delivery runs with automated Metrc manifests and multiple stops per route.
- **Payment Processing:** Cashless transactions with Flowhub Pay.
- **Analytics:** Dashboards available on mobile for off-site visibility.


### Flowhub Strengths


- **Mobile Scanning:** Handheld hardware purpose-built for intake and cycle counts.
- **Budtender Experience:** A clean sales interface that new staff pick up quickly.
- **Compliance Automation:** Metrc manifests for delivery routes generate without manual entry.


### Flowhub Weaknesses


- **Young E-Commerce Product:** The native store launched in July 2025, so feature depth and the integration catalog around it are still filling in.
- **Delivery Depends on a Second Platform:** Driver-side routing and live tracking run through Onfleet rather than Flowhub itself, which means a second contract and a second interface for your drivers.
- **No Dynamic Delivery:** Flowhub Delivery is built for store-based runs, not for vehicles carrying inventory and fulfilling on the road.
- **Back-Office Effort:** Operators report that reporting and reconciliation take more manual steps than front-of-house work does.

### E-Commerce


Both platforms now ship a native online store, so the question is what the store costs and how much of it you have to assemble.


- **Cova:** Cova eCommerce syncs inventory and pricing with the POS in real time, and is sold as a separate product from the core POS plan. Retailers wanting deeper storefront customization are pointed to Cova's e-commerce partners, and many operators continue running marketplace menus like[Weedmaps](https://getmeadow.com/integration-partners-weedmaps) or[Leafly](https://getmeadow.com/integration-partners-leafly) alongside it.
- **Flowhub:** The POS-native store launched in July 2025 with live inventory sync, the same discount and tax engine the POS uses, and ACH pre-payment. Flowhub does not publish pricing for it, so confirm how it lands on your invoice. It is the newest piece of the stack, so expect a shorter track record than the POS itself.
- **Meadow:** Customizable online menus and checkout, included in the platform fee rather than quoted as an add-on.


### Delivery Management


Delivery is where both platforms stop short of covering the job end to end, and where the second vendor appears. Cova takes delivery orders onto the same inventory and compliance ledger as in-store sales, and Cova's own guidance directs retailers to a logistics partner such as Carrot for dispatch and live vehicle tracking at scale. Flowhub Delivery runs store-based routes and generates Metrc manifests automatically, then hands the driver-side work to Onfleet. Neither supports the[ice cream truck model](https://getmeadow.com/blog/how-to-launch-mobile-dispensary-ice-cream-truck-delivery) , where drivers carry inventory and fulfill orders without returning to the store between stops.


Meadow runs both hub-and-spoke and dynamic delivery natively, with geofencing, automated dispatch, and real-time ledger compliance, so the delivery program and the POS share one system and one vendor.

### Compliance


All three platforms report to Metrc, and the difference is how much reconciliation work survives the automation. Cova runs a two-way Metrc integration that syncs sales in real time and applies adjustment reason codes automatically. Flowhub automates Metrc reporting including delivery manifests, though operators describe the reporting and reconciliation side as more manual than the sales side. Meadow syncs every sale to Metrc as it happens, with real-time ledger compliance covering delivery, so reconciliation stays an exception rather than a standing task. For the mechanics of that work, see[Metrc Reconciliation for Dispensaries](https://getmeadow.com/blog/metrc-reconciliation-for-dispensaries) .


### Inventory Management


Real-time tracking is table stakes across all three, so the separation is in counting tools and how many menus stay in sync. Cova offers batch scanning, bulk adjustments, room-level segmentation, and reorder reports. Flowhub pairs its Nug handheld with inventory counts, which gives floor staff a fast intake path, though reconciliation leans on manual steps. Meadow runs cycle counts, forecasting, and order reminders with real-time updates across every menu and channel at once.


### User Experience


All three are straightforward on the sales floor, and the friction shows up in the back office. Cova's interface is easy for budtenders to learn, though operators report lag and occasional crashes that frustrate staff when lines are longest. Flowhub's sales screen is clean and quick to train on, while back-office reporting takes more steps. Meadow runs front and back of house in one interface, which cuts training time and keeps managers out of a second system, backed by 99.999% uptime since 2014.

## The High Cost of Fragmented Systems


Fragmentation is not a philosophical problem, it is a line-item problem. When a platform covers a job partway, the gap gets filled with another subscription: a delivery logistics platform, an upgraded storefront, a separate analytics layer. That shows up as:


- **Added Cost:** Each add-on brings its own subscription, transaction fees, and renewal cycle.
- **Reconciliation Work:** Systems that sync imperfectly produce mismatches someone has to chase.
- **Training Load:** Staff learn two or three interfaces instead of one, and onboarding slows.
- **Slower Service:** Handoffs between disconnected systems surface as wait time at the counter and on the doorstep.


### The Long-Term Benefits of Choosing All-in-One


An all-in-one platform removes the seams between sales, inventory, compliance, and delivery, which is where most operational cost hides. One system means one set of numbers, one vendor to call when something breaks, and one interface to train on. As a dispensary adds locations or channels, that consolidation compounds: the work of opening a second store is mostly configuration rather than another round of vendor selection.

## Final Thoughts: Cova vs Flowhub


Cova and Flowhub are both credible choices for a retail-first dispensary, and the right answer depends on how much of your operation lives outside the sales counter. Cova brings a deep integration catalog, strong Metrc automation, and mature inventory tooling, with the online store quoted as its own product and a standing operator complaint about speed under load. Flowhub brings purpose-built scanning hardware, a fast budtender interface, and a newer native storefront that shares the POS pricing engine, with more of the back-office work done by hand.


The split that matters is delivery. Both platforms will take a delivery order, and neither carries the program end to end, so operators who deliver run a logistics vendor alongside the POS. That is a workable arrangement, and it is also the point where the stack stops being one system and starts being two, with the costs and reconciliation steps that follow.

## Common Questions


### Is Cova or Flowhub better for dispensaries?


It depends on where your operation is weighted. Cova suits retailers who want a deep integration catalog and mature inventory tooling and are comfortable buying the online store separately. Flowhub suits retailers who want purpose-built scanning hardware and a fast sales interface, and who can absorb more manual back-office work. Neither carries a delivery program end to end, so operators who deliver should compare both against an all-in-one platform.


### Do Cova and Flowhub have built-in e-commerce or delivery?


Both have native e-commerce. Cova eCommerce launched in late 2022 and is sold separately from the core POS plan; Flowhub's POS-native store launched in July 2025 and runs on the same discount and tax engine as the POS, though Flowhub does not publish pricing for it. Both also handle delivery orders, but dispatch, routing, and live driver tracking come from a partner platform in each case, and neither supports dynamic delivery.


### Do Cova and Flowhub work with Metrc?


Yes. Cova runs a two-way Metrc integration that reports sales in real time and syncs inventory adjustments with reason codes, and Flowhub automates Metrc reporting including delivery manifests. The practical difference operators notice is how much reconciliation is left over once the automation runs, which grows on stacks where sales, online orders, and delivery live in different systems.
